members.backstory: Simone framed houses. They can look at a tree and see the shelter inside it. Their hands are already building before their brain catches up. Simone grew up in Springfield, cornfields, lake wind, and rust-belt factory towns. Simone's grandfather Daniel worked the high school and never complained. Irving grew up in Duluth, cornfields, lake wind, and rust-belt factory towns. Betty, Irving's daughter, is with her other parent, or was. Ruth grew up in Toledo, cornfields, lake wind, and rust-belt factory towns. Gustave, Ruth's son, could name every truck on the road by sound. members.backstory: Hisham guided deer hunters through bottomland for eleven seasons. They read sign the way other people read headlines. The woods here are wrong, but wrong woods still have tracks. members.name: Zintle Tshabalala
members.backstory: Zintle was a glazier — windows, storefronts, the occasional shattered sliding door. She has handled enough glass to be gentle with everything. Zintle grew up in Gqeberha, highveld grass, thunderstorms at four, and the fynbos coast in the south. Lindiwe, Zintle's sister, was taken at the Scattering. The boring half, they said — my sister, boring. I think about that every day. Zintle's daughter Ofen

members.name: Nina Petrova
members.backstory: Nina kept a fleet of delivery vans alive past 300,000 miles each. She believes everything can be fixed — her scarred knuckles are the proof. Her grandparents came from Seville; she grew up hearing Spanish at home, and still understand more than she can say. She spent 1 year working overseas and picked up enough English to get by. Fixes what can't be fixed. Morale is a machine too.

members.name: Ingrid Vik
members.backstory: Ingrid rebuilt knees, shoulders, and backs at a sports clinic outside Trondheim. She knows exactly how far to push a healing body and when to stop. Her grandparents came from Columbus; she grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than she can say. Rebuilds broken bodies. Patient with everyone except herself.

members.name: Katarina Novak
members.backstory: Katarina covered city hall for a metro daily for eight years. She knows how to get a straight answer out of someone who is paid to dodge. She learned English on the job as a journalist. Was embedded in three war zones. The village is the fourth.

members.name: Henry Zhang
members.backstory: Henry took emergency calls for the district dispatch center, twelve-hour shifts of other people's worst days. He knows how to keep a caller breathing while the ambulance is still miles out. His parents came from Omaha; he grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than he can say. Priya's deputy. They reconcile the pantry. It's intense.

members.name: Theo Lindqvist
members.backstory: Theo led a trail crew in the national forest — six months a year of crosscut saws, switchbacks, and weather. He has slept under worse sky than this. His parents came from rural Vermont; he grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than he can say. Leo's mentor. Teaches speedrunning. Of what, unclear.

members.name: Leo Martin
members.backstory: Leo spent six seasons building trail through country most people only fly over. He has carried everything he owns on his back and liked it. Theo's sidekick. Learning speedrunning. Of what, unclear.

members.name: Naran Tumen
members.backstory: Naran is here. Drove the night bus in Ulaanbaatar. Says the village roads are shorter but the passengers are stranger.

members.name: Maleewan Chanarat
members.backstory: Maleewan delivered babies in farmhouse kitchens and cramped apartment bedrooms for twelve years. They know how to stay calm when everyone else is screaming. Maleewan grew up in Khon Kaen, paddy country, teak hills in the north, and long hot afternoons. Selin, Maleewan's grandmother, kept everything: letters, buttons, recipes. members.name: Yuki Mori
members.backstory: Yuki ran the reference desk at a branch library. She knows where every kind of knowledge lives. Now the library is gone and she is the reference desk. Cataloging the Codex. Dewey Decimal for the apocalypse.

members.name: Jesse Cortez
members.backstory: Jesse ran the fry station at a roadside diner. He can tell when oil is ready by the sound. He did the same math every shift: what feeds people, fast. Hannah's kitchen rival. Quiet. The food is loud enough.

members.name: Rafael Torres
members.backstory: Rafael was a roofer for fifteen summers in Medellín. He has never been afraid of heights, only of Mondays. His parents came from Manchester; he grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than he can say. Not afraid of heights. Afraid of idle hands.

members.name: Nolan ODonnell
